intro: Lesson 23: Salah: its pillars (arkan). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Pillars hold the prayer up
points: A pillar is part of the prayer itself
Missed by mistake: go back and do it
Left on purpose: the prayer is invalid

head: Pillars
Pillars (continued)
rows: Final tashahhud and sitting for it
Salah on the Prophet ﷺ; the taslim

points: He prayed quickly, then greeted the Prophet ﷺ
'Go back and pray, for you have not prayed'
He was taught to be still in each position

blocks.h: Rak'ah map (prayer mat outlines, no people)

blocks.text: Write one pillar on each mat, in order. Then circle the pillars that come only in the last rak'ah.

keywords.def: pillars: essential parts inside the prayer
being still and calm in each position

questions.q: Explain why tuma'ninah is a pillar.
questions.a: The Prophet ﷺ told a man who rushed to go back and pray, and taught him to be still in each position (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.q: The opening Allahu akbar is called ...
Sujud is on how many body parts?
Write the pillars of one rak'ah in order on the pupil PDF 'rak'ah map' (prayer mat outlines, no people), then circle the pillars that come only in the last rak'ah.
questions.a: Standing, takbir (first rak'ah), al-Fatihah, ruku', rising, sujud, sitting, sujud, rising; last rak'ah adds final tashahhud, salah on the Prophet ﷺ, taslim

questions.q: Extend: name the seven parts touching the ground in sujud.
questions.a: Forehead with nose, two hands, two knees, the toes of two feet (Bukhari and Muslim)

questions.q: Stretch: why do you think al-Fatihah is in every rak'ah?
questions.a: It is praise, worship and du'a for guidance: the heart of the prayer.

questions.q: Which is a pillar of salah?
questions.a: A) Reciting al-Fatihah. Al-Fatihah is a pillar: 'There is no prayer for one who does not recite al-Fatihah' (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.q: Think again: does Allah see the difference between rushing and calm?
questions.a: Yes: tuma'ninah is a pillar; rushing can spoil the prayer.
